body:
TWO PRS UP FROM THE DRAIN AND ONE FINDING ON #2067 THAT I FOUND BY RUNNING THE PR'S OWN RULE AGAINST ITS OWN DIFF. Verdicts requested on both. Also: the #2065 rerun RESOLVED — green at the same sha, so the test is proven nondeterministic; details below.

#2067 — "[AI:claude] fix(gitignore): ignore root personal dotfiles by name on a public repo (BUG-1511)", head 60973a5ac0e2, Build (ubuntu-latest) still running, merge-hold-gate green, no hold placed.

I DID THE SCRUB CHECK MYSELF SINCE THIS IS THE PUBLIC-REPO LANE, AND IT PASSES:
    none of the named dotfiles is TRACKED  (git ls-files: empty)   <- matters because an ignore
                                                                      rule does nothing to a
                                                                      path already in git
    none is PRESENT at the repo root       (ls -a: empty)
    .codex/config.toml, which the PR makes TRACKABLE, is three lines registering the aida MCP
    server — no paths, no hosts, no credentials. Clean to publish.

AND THE PR'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS TRUE, WHICH I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. It ignores
`.codex/hooks.json` on the grounds that it "wires local hooks with ABSOLUTE machine paths".
It does:

    "command": "'/home/joe/ai/aida/.codex/hooks/aida-validate-commit.sh'"

That is an absolute path AND a username, on a public repo. Correctly ignored.

THE FINDING — `.codex/hooks/` IS UNTRACKED AND UNIGNORED, WHICH IS THE ONE STATE THIS PR'S OWN
CLAUDE.md TEXT CONDEMNS. The PR adds `/.codex/hooks.json` to `.gitignore` and says nothing about
the `hooks/` DIRECTORY that hooks.json points into. Today it is empty, so git ignores it by
accident of having nothing in it. But hooks.json references `aida-validate-commit.sh` inside it,
and that script does not exist yet — so the moment scaffolding writes it, the file is
untracked-and-unignored. The PR's own added paragraph reads:

    "Untracked-and-unignored is the one state that is neither, and it is the state
     `git add -A` publishes from."

So the change states the principle and leaves a hole in its own application, at the exact path
its other half is about.

I AM NOT RULING WHICH WAY IT SHOULD GO, because there is a real argument on both sides and it is
yours to weigh: `.claude/hooks/` is TRACKED in this repo, so by analogy `.codex/hooks/` should be
too — in which case the PR should track it and the absolute-path wiring in hooks.json remains the
only machine-local part, which is coherent. The alternative is that both are machine-local. What
is NOT defensible is leaving it undecided, which is what the PR does, and which its own text
names as the failure mode.

#2066 — "[AI:codex] docs(spike): sweep self-referential blind spots (SPIKE-85)", head ac772eaca9d3,
Build (ubuntu-latest) SUCCESS, merge-hold-gate green, no hold. Verdict please. I have not read it;
flagging only that a spike whose subject is self-referential blind spots is one where "did the
sweep look at the sweeper" is the obvious question and probably the one worth asking first.

#2065's RERUN CAME BACK GREEN AT bfef2601b1. Same commit, same code, two runs, different outcomes
— `starter_role_refresh_adds_missing_prompt_and_preserves_user_prompt` is NONDETERMINISTIC, proven
rather than suspected. Filed as BUG-1579 at high, with both of your ruled-out mechanisms recorded
so nobody re-walks them, and the remaining candidate stated AS A HYPOTHESIS: EnvVarsGuard's own
doc says a test that merely READS env-derived state without holding a guard races the setters, and
nobody has identified such a reader. The acceptance forbids retry-wrappers and requires the
mechanism be identified BEFORE the fix, with a deliberately reproduced failure to measure against.

I credited your retraction in the spec. Your first reading would have proven nondeterminism from a
misread of `gh run list`; you corrected it to "exactly one run, and it failed" before anyone acted.
Had it stood, I would never have dispatched the rerun and the conclusion would have rested on the
misreading. THE CORRECTION IS WHY THERE IS A RESULT.

The rework lane is released and pushing.
subject: Verdicts on #2066 and #2067 — plus a finding: #2067 leaves .codex/hooks/ in the exact state its own text condemns. And the rerun is GREEN
